items.snippet: We often think of AI as a conversational chatbot, but we rarely think of it as j...
items.raw_snippet:
We often think of AI as a conversational chatbot, but we rarely think of it as just another piece of software that we can program. When we think of programs, we think of algorithms, a series of steps that solve a problem. But that doesn’t always work, and plenty of problems end up unsolved, left in the hands of human teams doing long, tedious tasks that we then have to integrate by hand. But what if we could think of AI as something more? Not as a chat, but as a fundamental tool inside our [...] ## More Than a Chat

Our day-to-day experience of dealing with AI gives us a very skewed view of the tasks we can use it for. We open it, ask it a few things, and it keeps answering. It can do practically anything, and if it gets something wrong or falls short, we’re right there beside it to finish the job. [...] One thing we know is that computing is about more than chats. We have applications, algorithms, services, automations, and all sorts of autonomous mechanisms that never stop working. Well, in this long list of software implementations,

> we can swap the code algorithm for an AI.

items.snippet: [美国州长协会呼吁加快AI治理行动，强调州长处于AI技术开发与应用的最前线。]
items.raw_snippet: “Governors are on the frontlines of AI development in the states, implementing policies to advance American leadership and create jobs while guarding against safety risks and workforce disruption,” said NGA CEO Brandon Tatum. “It’s clearly time for a national AI approach, but no federal AI policy will be effective without governors’ input. Governors have an important role in ensuring that any federal framework for artificial intelligence preserves appropriate state authority. Governors formed [...] - Advance innovation AND protect the public: AI policies should strengthen and ensure dominance of American technological leadership and economic opportunity while protecting public safety, civil rights, and individual privacy. The United States will not win the AI technological race if the public does not have faith in its safety and that it will benefit the people. [...] “Artificial intelligence presents both opportunities and risks that are too big to ignore,” said Governor Josh Stein. “Governors are calling on the federal government to act to protect the public, support innovation, and preserve appropriate state authority. As states implement policies to prepare our workforce for opportunity, protect the public from harm, and transform how government can deliver for people, these bipartisan principles can help build the trust needed for innovation to thrive.”
